verdict.rationale: Microsoft Authenticator documents a Cloud Backup feature for exactly this case: if you lose your phone or get a new device, you sign in to restore previously saved accounts and their one-time password codes. The documentation also covers the iCloud setup required on iOS. Caveats: backup covers only "eligible" accounts, needs a personal Microsoft account (a community user notes a paid business subscription doesn't count), and passkeys are device-bound so they never transfer. missing for 10: a documented list of which accounts are eligible, restore steps for passkeys and other non-eligible credentials, and independent hands-on confirmation that restore works.

support.subject: As an everyday user, losing my phone doesn't lose my accounts — a documented recovery path restores my tokens on a new device

citations.quote: This article describes how to back up information on all the accounts you have in Authenticator so that if you lose your mobile or get a new device, you can sign in to restore previously saved accounts
Turn on the Cloud Backup toggle. Select a Microsoft personal account where the backup will be stored.
Microsoft Authenticator backs up one-time password codes for eligible Microsoft personal accounts and third-party accounts, such as LinkedIn and Facebook.
To back up your Authenticator one-time password codes and account names on an iOS device, enable iCloud Drive, iCloud Keychain, and iCloud Backup for Authenticator.
